quotes.text: Restricted** MCCs may be supported, but require additional information at account creation.
Refunds for P24 payments are asynchronous and take up to 3 business days to complete. P24 refunds can’t be canceled.
After the payment completes, expand `latest_charge` on the PaymentIntent to retrieve the P24 reference number from `latest_charge.payment_method_details.p24.reference`.
Request the `p24_payments` capability and check that its status is `active` before accepting P24 payments.

old_evidence.text: Przelewy24 is a Poland-based payment method aggregator that allows customers to complete transactions online using bank transfers and other methods.
1Not supported when using Checkout in subscription mode or setup mode.2Available by invite only.
Payments made with Przelewy24 can only be submitted for refund within 180 days from the date of the original charge.

findings: Both guides describe a Poland-based aggregator for Polish customers in EUR or PLN, an established 40-business-location list, bank authentication/redirect, immediate payment notification, no recurring payments or chargebacks, full and partial refunds, and Dashboard or manual configuration routing. November gives domestic/crossborder labels, local settlement regions, and a stated 0.50 EUR minimum without supplying a PLN minimum (old raw lines 8-54,56-111,113-148,177-183, new raw lines 7-21,162-216,237-265,266-310). November describes both the aggregator and its bank-redirect family (new raw lines 7-15). The descriptors are compatible. Scope the parentheticals at source lines 13 and 18 to multiple underlying payment methods without implying exclusion from the bank-redirect family.

May labels the family authenticated bank debit and describes standard payout timing (old raw lines 12-38). November labels it bank redirects, with immediate confirmation, instant provisional access and settlement up to T+2 business days (new raw lines 7-15). Preserve the dated label change and distinguish payment confirmation, provisional access, settlement and merchant payout. No replatforming or payout SLA is established. May's 180 days is a refund submission limit, not a merchant return promise or completion time (old raw lines 177-183, new raw lines 208-231).

May asks for a publicly accessible website or app, priced product/service list, company identifiers and refund/privacy policy links, with a warning about suspension or termination for category or site violations (old raw lines 167-175). November lists a website beyond Stripe activation requirements, address/tax/registration, return and refund, privacy and terms of service; eligibility may be reviewed after activation and restrictions can be appealed through support (new raw lines 18-37). November omits the May priced-list and public-access wording and does not expressly withdraw it.

November retains the ten broadly prohibited categories and adds a code-level table treating prohibited MCCs as unsupported and restricted MCCs as potentially supported with additional information at account creation (old raw lines 150-175, new raw lines 18-37,39-160,174-190). The two rules overlap without a precedence explanation, such as broad pawn shops prohibited versus MCC 5933 restricted (new raw lines 138,184) and broad automotive prohibition versus MCC 5511 restricted (new raw lines 126,182). Connect marketplaces are a listed account type and Marketplace MCC 5262 is prohibited (new raw lines 19-22,55). Preserve those scopes and warn reciprocally rather than using a restricted or account-type cell to infer an exception or individual approval.

The November P24 page marks Billing and Invoicing supported, with a `send_invoice`-only collection note after the matrix (new raw lines 241-265). May's method page says Invoicing was invite-only, and Checkout setup/subscription modes were excluded (old raw lines 101-111). The same-date November Bank Redirects P24 row still says Invoicing invite-only, excludes Checkout setup and subscription modes, marks Subscriptions `send_invoice` only, and excludes SetupIntents, future usage and manual capture (raw/stripe-payments-bank-redirects-2026-11-07.md:25-34,38-50). Keep these support/access/collection distinctions and reciprocal warnings in P24 and Bank Redirects. Billing/invoice collection offers no evidence of recurring automatic P24 charges or unrestricted Invoicing access.

Separate the customer bank authorization, payment notification and merchant return from verified payment outcome and funds availability. The November customer flow adds completion of bank authorization within one hour of checkout (new raw lines 266-290). After payment completion, retrieve its P24 reference from an expanded PaymentIntent `latest_charge.payment_method_details.p24.reference`; the statement carries this reference and the custom pre-confirmation or account-default descriptor (new raw lines 292-302). The refund reference is a different field and can be shared after refund success if available (new raw lines 229-235). May explicitly calls browser return to the merchant optional (old raw lines 113-132). November lists browser return as step six without that qualifier (new raw lines 266-290). This wording difference leaves the requirement unresolved and does not establish a prerequisite for payment completion or a fulfillment signal.

November limits explicit Connect capability instructions to connected accounts with Express Dashboard or no Stripe-hosted Dashboard. Request `p24_payments` and verify `active` before accepting. Front-end Dashboard enablement lets Stripe determine relevant methods, and the manual route links the acceptance guide (new raw lines 304-310; old raw lines 134-148). Neither enablement nor a support cell proves account or transaction eligibility.
substantive_changes: Documented family changes from authenticated bank debit to bank redirects, and November specifies single-use, instant provisional access, immediate confirmation and up to T+2 settlement while May described standard payout timing (old raw lines 12-38, new raw lines 7-15). The 180-day submission window stays documented.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/p24 describes Przelewy24, a single-use bank-redirect aggregator. It serves Polish customers in EUR or PLN and lists eligible business locations and local settlement geography separately. It specifies a 0.50 EUR minimum, account and business categories, site disclosures, possible review, and additional information for restricted MCCs. The customer selects a bank and authorizes within one hour. Immediate confirmation and provisional access are separate from up-to-T+2 settlement, and a browser return alone does not verify payment or payout (new raw lines 7-39, new raw lines 162-216 and new raw lines 266-310). The page lists Checkout Sessions and PaymentIntents for one-time payments, excludes SetupIntents and setup_future_usage, and excludes recurring and manual capture. Express or no-Stripe-dashboard connected accounts need active p24_payments. The full or partial refund must be submitted within 180 days of the original payment. This is the payment method's maximum submission window, and the merchant return policy determines what it offers. The asynchronous, noncancelable refund is a separate bank credit and can take up to three business days. Check the Refund object's status. If the refund fails, the amount returns to the merchant's Stripe balance and the merchant must arrange an alternative refund. After a successful refund, share the Refund's optional `destination_details.p24.reference` if available. An original-payment P24 reference instead belongs to the PaymentIntent's latest Charge (new raw lines 217-235, new raw lines 241-265 and new raw lines 292-310). The May guide and source-stripe-p24.md preserve Polish buyers, EUR/PLN, merchant geography, no recurring or chargebacks, refund window, prohibited categories and website rules. The November guide expands these and the baseline should label 180 days as a submission window (old raw lines 8-54, old raw lines 56-111 and old raw lines 150-183).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/p24, the November capture adds substantive documented eligibility and MCC rules, website terms, account review and appeal, local settlement geography and a 0.50 EUR minimum, the authorization window, fuller UI/API boundaries, a connected-account capability condition, refund status and payment/refund reference handling (new raw lines 18-190, new raw lines 208-265 and new raw lines 266-310). The unchanged ten broad categories coexist with a prohibited/restricted MCC list and some overlapping labels. Carry the conflict reciprocally in P24 and avoid treating restricted codes or Connect marketplace support as clearance. May's authenticated-bank-debit label, standard payout wording, publicly accessible site/app, product prices, suspension, Checkout mode exclusions and invite-only Invoicing need dated retention in source-stripe-p24.md (old raw lines 12-54, old raw lines 101-111 and old raw lines 150-183). November's bank-redirect label and T+2 settlement do not establish a different payment mechanism or external payout schedule. The method page lists Billing/Invoicing with a send_invoice collection note, while the same-date Bank Redirects matrix retains invite-only Invoicing and checkout-mode exclusions and scopes Subscriptions to send_invoice. Warn reciprocally without inferring automatic recurring billing or an invitation waiver. Replacing flow artwork with headings and changing the navigation links are presentational. The November one-hour authorization condition is substantive. May explicitly calls browser return to the merchant optional (old raw lines 113-132). November lists browser return as step six without that qualifier (new raw lines 266-290). This wording difference leaves the requirement unresolved and does not establish a prerequisite for payment completion or a fulfillment signal. November describes both the aggregator and its bank-redirect family (new raw lines 7-15). The descriptors are compatible. Scope the parentheticals at source lines 13 and 18 to multiple underlying payment methods without implying exclusion from the bank-redirect family. The separate May 3, 2026 acceptance guide gives a 14-character statement descriptor limit (raw/stripe-p24-accept-payment-2025.md:1-4,259-261). Keep that limit dated to that implementation authority. The November overview describes the pre-confirmation descriptor, its account-level fallback, and the original-payment reference without specifying a length (new raw lines 292-302). Keep bank authorization, browser return, payment confirmation, settlement, and final Refund status distinct.
